title: Wall Street Punishes Tech Stocks on Earnings Misses

notes.headline: Nasdaq 100 plunges 4% into correction as Intel and Amazon fuel AI capex fears
notes.summary: US equity markets experienced a severe tech-led sell-off, with the Nasdaq 100 entering a technical correction after falling 4% in a single session. Intel's 31% plunge and Amazon's slowing retail growth triggered a rotation into defensive sectors like energy and utilities, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 9%. Investors are increasingly questioning the return on massive AI capital expenditures as market volatility, measured by the VIX, spiked above 23.
key_takeaways: Nasdaq 100 fell over 4%, marking a 10% technical correction from its October peak.
Intel plummeted roughly 31% after issuing weak Q4 guidance and reporting factory yield challenges.
Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) plunged approximately 9% as semiconductor sentiment soured.
Amazon dropped ~2.5% due to slowing 2% e-commerce growth and high AI capex, despite strong AWS projections.
VIX spiked above 23, signaling a significant breakout in market stress levels.
Crude oil (WTI) rose above $104/bbl on geopolitical tensions, while Gold fell 3.5% to ~$3,882/oz.
ICE CEO Jeff Sprecher announced plans for 23/5 US equity trading starting in December to meet retail demand.
macro: Geopolitical conflicts in the Persian Gulf and Russia supported crude oil prices and buoyed oil company refining results.
US Treasury yields remained elevated: 2-year near 4.56%, 10-year near 4.92%, and 30-year at 5.30%.
Market breadth deteriorated sharply, prompting a flight to cash-flow safety in defensive dividend payers.
priced_in: Markets are no longer rewarding AI hype; immediate ROI and positive free cash flow are now required for valuation support.
Nasdaq 100 has priced in a full 10% technical correction from recent highs.
Street had priced in strong AI growth for semiconductors, leaving Intel vulnerable after failing to deliver high-margin beats.
fundamentals: Intel: Q4 revenue guided to $15B-$16B vs. $17B consensus; facing factory yield issues and market share losses to AMD.
Amazon: Online retail sales rose only 2% to $68.5B; company arranged an $80B supplier financing facility for AI hardware.
Big Oil: ExxonMobil, Chevron, Shell, BP, and TotalEnergies reported combined adjusted net income of $56.3B, beating expectations.
Reddit: Plunged ~30% following plans to restrict open forum access to drive user registrations.

Yields held relatively steady with 10-year yields around 4.92% and 30-year yields above 5.30%.
